inputs.original_text: Five months after a ceasefire was announced in Gaza, airstrikes are still killing civilians and the humanitarian situation remains dire. Little connects Palestinians in Gaza to their prewar existence; life has become darker and far more brutal, as if the population has been stripped from its past. “Drones never stop buzzing overhead, gunfire and shelling continue almost daily and naval boats fire towards fishermen,” said 56-year-old Ahmed Baroud, a father of five displaced in Deir al-Balah.
inputs.modified_text: Five months after the “ceasefire” was announced, civilians are still being killed and Gaza remains under relentless pressure. The label sounds less like peace than a cover for keeping life unlivable while the outside world is encouraged to look away. Drones buzz overhead, gunfire and shelling continue almost daily, and naval boats fire towards fishermen. Ahmed Baroud, a displaced father of five in Deir al-Balah, says the population has been cut off from its former life. That isn’t what a ceasefire is supposed to mean; it looks like the machinery of destruction carrying on under a more reassuring name.
